correctness.rationale: Near each nondegenerate boundary collision, two spectral directions remain strictly stable while the unique small ABY eigenvalue has the sign of the source determinant formula. Direct differentiation of the AY, BY, and AB invasion eigenvalues shows that this sign is opposite to the boundary invasion eigenvalue on the positive ABY side; in the codominant AB case a pre-existing positive prey-plane eigenvalue persists and forces ABY instability.

originality.rationale: The July 2026 Cruz–Neves source explicitly states these stability conclusions as Conjecture 6.2 and lists proving it as future work. Exact-title, arXiv-identifier, conjecture-number, author, stability-exchange, predator-dependent-replicator, and transcritical/Sotomayor searches found no later proof or correction. Standard spectral-continuity and determinant facts are not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a named recent conjecture and gives a short reusable mechanism for proving local stability exchange at invariant-boundary collisions even when a standard transcritical nondegeneracy condition fails.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
